facts.value: The Master's program in Southeast Asian Studies offers students who have knowledge of the Indonesian or Malaysian language and are familiar with the Southeast Asian region the opportunity to deepen their understanding of the cultures, societies, and languages of Southeast Asia. The focus is on the Malay world (Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Brunei, and East Timor). The goal of this research-oriented Master's program is to enable independent research at an advanced level. The Master's program deepens and complements the methods learned in the Bachelor's program and enables students to critically reflect on them, as well as engage with theoretical concepts of their own field and relate these to generally discussed theories and research developments. Students are instructed in cultural scientific analysis and scientific work.
The Master's program in Southeast Asian Studies can be studied in two different variants. Variant 2 differs from Variant 1 by including an integrated semester abroad.

Students in Variant 1 are allowed to set individual content focuses in the elective area, such as the following suggested profiles: classical philology and history of the Malay world, modern language application and society in the Malay world, culture and economy in Southeast Asia.
